items.why: The report lists an extra band at "358.3" (4 K) and "357.6" (80 K) on the high side of Ag3 but never mentions a ~220 cm-1 shoulder or Ag2 asymmetry, and it does not call either feature a new low-temperature feature.

The band lists show the ~358 cm-1 band at 4 K and 80 K and missing at 150 K and 300 K, but the report does not say it is weaker at 80 K and makes no link to the Néel temperature, magnetic order or spin-phonon coupling.
The report assigns no symmetry to any band; the 358 cm-1 band is only listed as "bands at ... 358.3" and is never called B3g.

The fitted positions show both main bands moving up on cooling (237.0→242.0 and 338.4→341.4; "strongest band of 4 K shifts by -2.99 cm-1 in 300 K"), but the report never states the narrowing trend or that Ag2 broadens more than Ag3.
The caveats list is empty, and the report never mentions anharmonic or multiphonon effects as an alternative explanation.
The report says nothing about intensities depending on the circular polarization configuration.
"questions_for_user" is empty, so the report asks neither for finer temperature steps nor for a bulk reference.

wrong_claims.why: The 150 K and 300 K band lists ("240.1, 300.8, 340.6" and "237.0, 338.4") contain no band near 220 or 355 cm-1.
The report gives higher frequencies at low temperature (338.4 at 300 K vs 341.4 at 4 K), which is hardening on cooling, not softening.
